newsitem.title: USA: Centennial ex-CEO assets frozen indefinitely.
newsitem.headline: Centennial ex-CEO assets frozen indefinitely.

text.p: The assets of Centennial Technologies Inc's former chief executive were indefinitely frozen by a U.S. federal judge on Monday.

U.S. District Judge Patti Saris granted a motion submitted by the Securities and Exchange Commission to extend a temporary restraining order freezing the assets of Emanuel Pinez, who was arrested earlier this month for securities fraud.
Saris also ordered a March 6 hearing to allow Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc to present objections to the restraining order raised by the firm on Monday. Lehman did not elaborate on its objections.
Pinez, who allegedly engaged in insider trading by buying and selling puts and calls on Centennial stock, owed Lehman more than $5.4 million when the account was frozen, according to court records.

Last week, Saris agreed to modify the temporary restraining order to allow Lehman Brothers and PaineWebber Group Inc, which also claims it is owed millions of dollars, to liquidate Pinez's accounts to settle an estimated $21 million debt.

Lawyers for PaineWebber and for Chicago options traders who claim to have lost about $3.75 million as a result of Pinez's trades, told the court on Monday that they supported the extension of the restraining order.
Also on Monday, Saris agreed to amend the restraining order to allow Saugus, Mass.-based PG Technologies, a privately held personal computer memory card company, to access a frozen bank account.

The $14,000 account, used for payrolls and general expenses, was frozen because Pinez, who invested $400,000 in the PG Technologies last year, had signatory powers over the funds, said Frances DiMento, a lawyer for the company.
"I'm not going to close this company down. I'm going to pay this company's payroll," Saris said.
Gil Peretz, the president of PG Technologies, took the stand to tell the court the purpose of the account, though he later declined to tell reporters about his relationship with Pinez.
